sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
There is no dashboard. `next` returns one item, `stats` returns counts, and the blocked
set only appears inside `next`'s empty-queue payload. A user starting their day runs three
commands and stitches the answer — what is next, what is done of the total, what is
blocked on what — in their head. It is also the natural "did it work" command after
`init`.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: - `src/slicer/cli.py` — a new `status` command composing existing ops

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `status` shows the next item, a census, and the blocked edges.
2. `status --json` carries all three.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
A `status` command that composes `next`, the `stats` census, and the blocked list into
one view and one `--json` payload. Pure composition of existing `ops`; no new state.

**Not in this slice:** a TUI dashboard — this is the CLI front door.
